old:
Latin texts: • "providentia quidem cuncta pariter quamvis diversa quamvis infinita complectitur" (IV.6.10)
  (Providence embraces all things together though diverse and infinite)
• "fatum vero singula digerit in motum locis formis ac temporibus distributa" (IV.6.11)
  (Fate arranges individual things in motion, distributed by place, form, and time)
new:
Latin text (Cons. IV.pr.6): • "immobilem simplicemque gerendarum formam rerum esse providentiam, fatum vero eorum quae divina simplicitas gerenda disposuit mobilem nexum atque ordinem temporalem"
  (Providence is the immovable and simple form of things to be done; Fate is the moving connection and temporal order of those things which the divine simplicity has disposed to be done)
